newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian composer Denisov dead at 67.
newsitem.headline: Russian composer Denisov dead at 67.

text.p: Russian avant-garde composer Edison Denisov, who was ignored by Soviet authorities but won acclaim in the West, has died at the age of 67, Itar-Tass news agency said on Monday.
Denisov had been ill for some time following a serious car accident near Moscow. He died in Paris after going to France for an operation.

Born in Tomsk in 1929, he studied piano and composition at the Moscow Conservatory, where he later taught. His first major work, "Soleil des Incas" (Sun of the Incas), was a prizewinner at the 1964 Darmstadt Festival.
Denisov, praised by colleagues for refusing to bow to official pressure in the Brezhnev years, spent time at the Electronic Music Research Centre in the late 1960s.
His works included the 1981 opera "L'Ecume des Jours" and the ballet "Confession" in 1984, as well as choral music and instrumental pieces.
